note: The first byte of the raw fuzz input controls the platform index; candidate byte 0x1a selects entry 26.
The selector is reduced modulo the platform table length; 0x1a remains 26 and maps to MOS65XX.
Detail mode is enabled, so the MOS65XX disassembler later fills detail fields but the printer also runs for the instruction.

code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
note: The remaining input bytes are passed as machine code; candidate byte 0xea is the MOS65XX NOP opcode.
A fresh MCInst is initialized for the decoded instruction before architecture-specific decoding.
Initialization marks each operand invalid but does not initialize the union payload ImmVal; later code can read an indeterminate value from an invalid operand slot.
For opcode 0xea (NOP), the addressing mode is implied and the instruction length is one byte.
Because len is 1, neither this branch nor the following len == 3 branch creates operand 0, leaving Operands[0].ImmVal as initialized only by MCInst_Init.
The implied addressing mode takes the MOS65XX_AM_IMP case and does not read Operands[0].ImmVal while filling details.
After successful decoding, Capstone invokes the MOS65XX printer with the MCInst whose operand 0 payload was never initialized.
The printer unconditionally reads operand 0's ImmVal before checking the addressing mode; for one-byte implied instructions this is a use of an uninitialized union member.
